open_errors.issue: In ch 25 Ila caches all five sheets in the gap behind the plank shelf of the second lake hut, and in ch 28 she tells Kunal they are still there. Neither of them goes back to the huts before the Under-Cairn, yet in ch 30 she reaches for the sheets in her coat and in ch 31 she copies them at Kothi Shilak. Ch 29 also says Kunal cut her crutch 'at the lake huts', a visit that never happens on the page.
open_errors.fix: Have Gauri, who was sitting at the cleft mouth within earshot, bring the sheets back from the hut with the lamp and bread, and have the crutch cut at the cleft mouth from a limb she carries up.

patches.find: Gauri came back when the light had gone grey. She had a lamp under her arm, a skin of oil and a cloth sack that smelled of bread. She set them down in a row, the way a woman lays out a trader's goods, and looked anywhere but the rope.
patches.replace: Gauri came back when the light had gone grey. She had a lamp under her arm, a skin of oil, a cloth sack that smelled of bread, and a thin oilcloth packet that she put into Ila's lap. "From behind the plank shelf," she said. "Sound carries at the mouth." She set the rest down in a row, the way a woman lays out a trader's goods, and looked anywhere but the rope.

patches.find: Kunal had cut the crutch at the lake huts, in the grey light, with his knife in his bad hand and Gauri holding the other end.
patches.replace: Kunal had cut the crutch at the cleft mouth, in the grey light, from a juniper limb Gauri carried up from the lake huts, with his knife in his bad hand and Gauri holding the other end.

open_errors.issue: Ch 16 says Ila swore her archive oath before the council clerk in the Garh Neshar hall, on a page that came with the summer post. Ch 23 says she swore it 'in a hall in Taravan'. Ila has not left Neshar since Book 1.
open_errors.fix: Change the ch 23 location to the Garh Neshar hall.

patches.find: She had sworn in a hall in Taravan to keep what the crown's papers held
patches.replace: She had sworn in the Garh Neshar hall to keep what the crown's papers held

open_errors.issue: Ch 20 takes place on the same day as ch 17's third morning (ch 17 morning, then ch 18 at the Eye, ch 19 at the lower huts, ch 20 that night). Ch 20 twice calls it twelve days of the bond, but ch 17 counts ten. Ch 13, three days of travel earlier, says six days, although the route from the binding to the basin (Ranu, Stair, plateau, Ewe's Rest, the Hollow Moon, two storm nights, the Ladder) takes about nine.
open_errors.fix: Make ch 13 nine days and ch 17 twelve days (twelve strokes, twenty-three left), so the counts agree with ch 20 and with day 16 at the Shilak Cairn.

patches.find: He had watched her for six days now and it had not once grown ordinary.
patches.replace: He had watched her for nine days now and it had not once grown ordinary.

patches.find: But she had spent six days learning his habits.
patches.replace: But she had spent nine days learning his habits.

patches.find: He had been looking at ten days of Ila's field book, and for the first time in his life he understood
patches.replace: He had been looking at twelve days of Ila's field book, and for the first time in his life he understood

patches.find: I've shown you three ways in ten days, and you're alive.
patches.replace: I've shown you three ways in twelve days, and you're alive.

patches.find: Ten. Ten strokes, and twenty-five empty places, and at the end of them the rope came off.
patches.replace: Twelve. Twelve strokes, and twenty-three empty places, and at the end of them the rope came off.

open_errors.issue: Meera knocks on the morning after Ila and Kunal come up at the Shilak Cairn, and ch 31 calls that morning 'the seventeenth day of the rope, the morning after the Under-Cairn'. Meera says 'Day sixteen. Nineteen days'.
open_errors.fix: Make Meera's count day seventeen, with eighteen days to the meadow (still day 35).

patches.find: "Day sixteen," said Meera. "Nineteen days to your meadow, if it's a soft year. Nineteen days your promise bites. After that it's only you."
patches.replace: "Day seventeen," said Meera. "Eighteen days to your meadow, if it's a soft year. Eighteen days your promise bites. After that it's only you."

open_errors.issue: In ch 3 thirty-five days is the gap between the Meadow and Shilak thaws ('I have the winter minus thirty-five days'). From ch 17 onward, thirty-five days is the bond's own length from the binding to the Meadow meltwater, and the actual gap in ch 31 is twenty-one days.
open_errors.fix: Have Ila's ch 3 figure be the bond's length in a soft year, not the gap.

patches.find: "Thirty-five days," she said. "In a soft year. That's what I lose."
patches.replace: "Thirty-five days," she said. "In a soft year. That's all the rope gives me."

patches.find: "The crown thinks I have the whole winter. I have the winter minus thirty-five days." She shut the book.
patches.replace: "The crown thinks I have the whole winter. I have thirty-five days of it." She shut the book.

open_errors.issue: Ila hedges that the letter 'did not say he had walked this way, only that he had been guided'. The ch 16 letter says plainly that Udai guided Harish 'by the way that begins at these lakes'. What it does not say is what Udai did.
open_errors.fix: Correct the hedge to match the letter's actual content.

patches.find: Hedged, even in her own head: the letter did not say he had walked this way, only that he had been guided.
patches.replace: Hedged, even in her own head: the letter said he had been guided this way, not what his guide had done.

open_errors.issue: In ch 20 Ila leaves the wrappings on Kunal's raw fingertips. The next morning in ch 21 his hands are 'bandaged to the knuckle, and the tips were pink', as if the tips were bare.
open_errors.fix: Keep the tips wrapped, with the pink showing at the edges.

patches.find: They were bandaged to the knuckle, and the tips were pink.
patches.replace: They were bandaged to the knuckle, and the tips showed pink at the edges of their wrappings.

open_errors.issue: At dawn Kunal says Ranu is 'a day down the Garh road', but the chapter opens with them already in Ranu at noon the same day.

patches.find: Then he turned south. "Ranu is a day down the Garh road.
patches.replace: Then he turned south. "Ranu is half a day down the Garh road.
